title: SIFMA-recommended 3:00 p.m. JST early close for the Tokyo session of the USD bond market — UK Easter Monday, on the day a BoJ Summary of Opinions publishes
source: NEWS: sifma.org/resources/guides-playbooks/holiday-schedule ('Holiday Schedule'), fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 298,926 bytes) and parsed out of the page's embedded Next.js flight payload by this session — the 2027 panels sit behind a year tab that a rendered-DOM parse never reaches, which is why the three sifma-* entries filed off this page before today are all 2026 or were read from the US panel. 121 cards recovered across all six panels; the Japan 2027 panel's Easter Monday card reads exactly ['Easter Monday', 'Early Close Only (3:00 p.m. Japan Standard Time): Monday, March 29, 2027 - Tentative - Subject to confirmation by the Bank of Japan']. The causing holiday is independently statutory: gov.uk/bank-holidays.json (HTTP 200, 22,207 bytes, England-and-Wales division) lists '2027-03-29 | Easter Monday'. Filed estimate on four counts: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for a trade association's recommended schedule, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, the source is NON-BINDING BY ITS OWN TERMS (a recommendation to members, not exchange hours), and SIFMA'S OWN CARD MARKS IT TENTATIVE — every card on the 2027 Japan panel carries the 'Subject to confirmation by the Bank of Japan' flag while no card on the 2026 panel does.
notes: DISCOVERED during the sifma-japan-early-close-2026-12-28 initial research (2026-09-05). WHY IT EARNS A ROW: it is the same configuration as the 2026-12-28 entry, recurring on a date this calendar ALREADY tracks a BoJ document for (boj-summary-of-opinions-2027-03-29, published 08:50 JST). SCOPE, stated because the 2026-12-28 entry was originally filed with the wrong reading of it: SIFMA's page says verbatim that 'All SIFMA holiday recommendations apply to the trading of U.S. dollar-denominated government securities...', so the Japan panel is a TIME ZONE, not an asset class — this is the Tokyo session of the US DOLLAR bond market closing early, and JGBs are out of scope entirely. THE RULE IT INSTANTIATES: every 'Early Close Only (3:00 p.m. Japan Standard Time)' card SIFMA publishes across 2026 and 2027 is a UK-ONLY bank holiday — 2026-04-06 Easter Monday, 2026-08-31 Summer Bank Holiday, 2026-12-28 Boxing Day, this one, and 2027-08-30 — while a US holiday shuts Tokyo's dollar desk in full and a UK-only holiday that is already a Japanese market holiday gets no card at all. SIFMA names the Tokyo card after the FOREIGN holiday that causes it. IMPACT LOW: nothing Japanese is shortened — JPX's own hours page puts OSE JGB futures at 08:45-11:00 and 12:30-15:00 with a 15:02 closing auction and a 15:30-05:55 night session, so 15:00 JST is where the listed day session already ends — no house playbook is calendar-, holiday- or rates-keyed (both playbook docs grepped this session for 'holiday|jpx|tokyo|nikkei|closure|year-end|new year|jgb|gilt|boxing|sifma': zero hits), and this repo tracks no Japan-listed symbol or JGB instrument. HONEST LIMIT: the 2027 panel is tentative throughout and its year-end section is internally inconsistent (its Boxing Day card reads 'None' though gov.uk dates a 2027-12-28 substitute, and its UK Christmas card reads 'Friday, December 24, 2027' rather than gov.uk's Monday substitute), so this date is more likely than the 2026 entries to move. RECORDED BUT NOT PROPOSED, from the same panel: 'Early Close Only (3:00 p.m. Japan Standard Time): Monday, August 30, 2027' (UK Summer Bank Holiday) — equally real, equally tentative, but with nothing co-dated on this calendar to make it material.
